dimension_policy.novelty: Only an O-overlap observation is recorded here; formal novelty classification remains owned by the separate novelty comparator.
dimension_policy.evidence_strength: No evidence-strength tier is assigned here. Evidence is referenced only to the originating clean worker artifact; separate evidence-comparator outputs are not judgment inputs.
dimension_policy.decision_relevance: Judged from current O read-only state using mechanism fit, expected decision-changing information value, implementation/evaluation tractability, overlap with O, active uncertainty, and expected elapsed-time impact.

input_integrity_note.handling: Only filenames/change presence were incidentally visible while locating the post-delta clean-worker wave. Their contents were excluded from all relevance judgments. No comparator or integrator result was fed back to exploration.

active_decision_context: O minimizes defensible expected elapsed time to genuine real-world AGI, is instrumental/replaceable, and may not weaken evidence integrity or the user's achievement standard.
Generation 12 is checkpointed; inbox revision 22 is acknowledged; exactly one current immutable Execute request remains pending for the revision-22 action-adherence comparison.
The pending unit must compare actual action traces for the current Context Kernel route versus a manifest-free control under frozen matched conditions; static/verbal understanding is not sufficient.

O already has scoped reversible Candidates, immutable invocation/effect journals, source clocks, dependency bindings, held-out machinery, critical dispatch rechecks, and exact negative-evidence scope policy.
Zero independent external production evidence remains a major bottleneck.
Only the clean_g1 research feed may be ingested at safe boundaries, and feed handling must not create extra Work invocations solely for polling.

highest_current_value_clusters: statistically valid and lineage-aware acceptance for repeated self-improvement, including activation/validity gates, optional-stopping control, adaptive-holdout protection, and false-commit budgets
behavioral deployment evaluation that separates monitor accuracy from intervention benefit, outcome success from procedural validity, and average capability from repeated-run reliability
transactional external-effect semantics and rollback boundaries: internal state restoration must not imply reversal of irreversible world effects
evaluation validity under ranking/Best-of-N selection, abstention, per-instance uncertainty, benchmark resolution, citation criteria, and retrieval-depth stress
adaptive resource allocation: conditional workflow depth, finite-budget evaluation allocation, cost-sensitive proxy experiments, and task-conditioned search routing
Context Kernel behavioral economics: compression/retrieval reacquisition cost, boundary-local action continuity, and optional-memory utilization rather than mere storage/retrieval
important_non_immediate_clusters: weight-training and biological local-credit mechanisms remain low relevance until O has a concrete training substrate and matched evaluation path
continual-pretraining schedules/replay and task-free adapter routing remain mostly low-to-low-medium for current O despite useful protocol/evidence-quality lessons
Lean-specific diversity/training mechanisms are useful search-control evidence but should not be promoted to O-wide architecture without compute-matched cross-domain tests

self_improvement.o_fit: O already uses held-out/regression gates and is currently testing action adherence, but it has not demonstrated the full validity→activation→statistical-credit decomposition for autonomous artifact changes.
self_improvement.scope: GSME/HarnessBank agent-harness evolution: six sealed-test domains in v1; v2 TB2 gate/archive studies. Selective-recovery LiveCode evidence and paired-significance results apply only to the reported harness/task/model conditions.
self_improvement.uncertainty: The no-archive causal effect of semantic QD is not isolated; validity lacks a standalone matched ablation; SWE-bench v1 result is preliminary at n=26. Gate effects may differ with O's deterministic/mechanical evaluators.
self_improvement.decision_use: Instrument Candidate credit as environment validity, mechanism activation/adherence, paired outcome evidence, and false-elite/archive hygiene before attributing improvement.

self_improvement.o_fit: O has method-change and saturation triggers, but task-conditioned stopping of self-improvement depth is not yet behaviorally calibrated.
self_improvement.scope: VeRO agent optimization budgets B∈{2,4,8,16,32}; GAIA held-out peaks near B=8 then falls at B=32 while TAU-Bench Retail continues improving. Results are benchmark/harness specific.
self_improvement.uncertainty: GAIA decline co-varies with search-trajectory entropy collapse and prompt-centric drift, so it is not a pure dev-set-overuse ablation; several tasks show flat rather than inverted-U behavior.
self_improvement.decision_use: Treat improvement horizon as an evidence-conditioned decision: measure marginal held-out benefit/cost and stop or change method when additional optimization loses value.

self_improvement.o_fit: O repeatedly evaluates and selects Candidates on protected evidence; adaptive reuse of the same gate can itself become an optimization target.
self_improvement.scope: Dwork et al. adaptive-data-analysis mechanism plus the worker's agent-specific VeRO/SkillOpt bridge. The >63% null-holdout artifact at k=500 is a classical synthetic demonstration, not an O or LLM-agent result.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Differential-privacy/Thresholdout machinery is not shown to transfer directly to O; the right leakage model and cost tradeoff for agent traces are untested.
self_improvement.decision_use: Track acceptance-query reuse and preserve a genuinely fresh terminal audit path; test bounded query budgets, rotating/growing canaries, or anytime-valid alternatives before trusting long adaptive lineages.

self_improvement.o_fit: Bounded edits, rejected-change memory, slow consolidation, and selection gates closely match O's scoped Candidate lifecycle and protected fallback philosophy.
self_improvement.scope: SkillOpt's 52 model×benchmark×harness cells and GPT-5.5 component ablations; selection split is reused for four adaptive epochs and final test is separate.
self_improvement.uncertainty: There is no matched no-validation-gate ablation, and the same selection set is repeatedly queried; final artifacts usually contain only 1–4 accepted edits, limiting conclusions about long-run gate integrity.
self_improvement.decision_use: Use SkillOpt as external support for bounded reversible edits and negative-feedback retention, while separately testing gate overuse and lineage-wide error control.

self_improvement.o_fit: O has protected held-out comparison but no demonstrated per-candidate optional-stopping certificate that explicitly controls false commits while allowing early stopping.
self_improvement.scope: PACE prompt-level self-evolution on Qwen2.5 0.5B–3B over GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC-Challenge; greedy false/harmful modification rates and ~18% evaluation-cost saving are specific to the reported controlled setup.
self_improvement.uncertainty: The reported guarantee is per candidate/decision, not automatically familywise over an unbounded adaptive lineage; testbed is small and prompt-level, and the worker notes detailed full-text verification remains incomplete.
self_improvement.decision_use: Prototype paired candidate/incumbent anytime-valid acceptance where evaluation is stochastic or sequential, but do not mistake per-decision control for run-level safety.

self_improvement.o_fit: O's long-running Candidate lineage lacks a demonstrated global false-commit budget/certificate ledger across an open-ended sequence of accepted self-edits.
self_improvement.scope: SEA's 52-instance SWE-bench Verified subset, four base models, and architecture for horizon-free confirm-triggered harmonic spending plus immutable certificates.
self_improvement.uncertainty: The paper explicitly leaves full familywise safety under endogenous proposal and edit-induced distribution shift unproved; several slow-loop guarantees are offline simulations, results are single-run, and weight-level training is not executed.
self_improvement.decision_use: Evaluate an immutable cumulative acceptance-risk ledger as a falsifiable Candidate mechanism, with fresh audit evidence and explicit abstention when endogenous-distribution assumptions fail.

self_improvement.o_fit: O optimizes elapsed time and expensive evidence acquisition; anytime-valid adaptive sampling could lower evaluation cost without converting repeated peeking into invalid confidence.
self_improvement.scope: CELEUS sequential LLM evaluation on SST-2/MMLU/AG News: e-process miscoverage 0.021–0.030 versus 0.161 for CER-EVAL at nominal alpha=.05; median evaluated samples reduced 54–62% at epsilon=.05 in reported settings.
self_improvement.uncertainty: CELEUS estimates one system's score/precision; it does not solve candidate-vs-incumbent multiplicity or proposer adaptation. Surrogate-guided acquisition could bias O if its conditional-unbiasedness assumptions fail.
self_improvement.decision_use: Test CELEUS-like adaptive sampling only inside a separately valid Candidate-comparison/risk-accounting protocol, measuring coverage and rollout cost under O's actual outcome distribution.

self_improvement.o_fit: Global error allocation across recursive edits is a direct missing complement to O's reversible Candidate acceptance when many sequential hypotheses are tested.
self_improvement.scope: SGM CIFAR-10/100/ImageNet-100 and RL/black-box studies under bounded paired differences and stable evaluation; CTHS concentrates global delta on confirmation events.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Validated scope is small/mid-scale ML rather than LLM-agent loops; guarantees depend on bounded i.i.d. paired differences and a stable harness, with heavy tails, correlation, drift, and endogenous adaptation outside scope.
self_improvement.decision_use: Use as a statistical design prior for lineage-level false-commit accounting, not as a proven drop-in guarantee; require O-specific matched tests and retain abstention/fallback.

long_horizon.o_fit: O already distinguishes observation from effect authorization, but this evidence directly tests whether an accurate monitor should trigger intervention and shows the answer can reverse by failure prevalence/domain.
long_horizon.scope: Failure-prediction study with 0.6B critic AUROC .936/F1 .963 across 1,372 held-out steps and matched deployment on HotPotQA/GAIA/ALFWorld across tested backbones.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Recovery/disruption rates are environment/backbone dependent; threshold sweeps did not rescue HotPotQA, but high-failure ALFWorld improved. This is not a universal anti-intervention result.
long_horizon.decision_use: Gate interventions on matched final-task A/B outcomes and explicit recovery-versus-disruption economics, not critic accuracy alone; permit no-op as a first-class policy.

long_horizon.o_fit: O already binds context to effects and uses idempotency/revocation checks, but external settlement semantics remain an explicit architecture boundary; Atomix directly measures that boundary.
long_horizon.scope: Atomix GPT-4.1 τ-bench/WebArena/OSWorld fault injection and 500 irreversible-send trials. Pure recoverable task success can be statistically tied to checkpoint replay; irreversible-effect leakage separates strongly.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Atomix cannot protect incorrectly classified/unmediated effects, does not provide distributed exactly-once semantics, and compensation is not reversal. Its strongest claim is effect-class-aware settlement, not generic transaction superiority.
long_horizon.decision_use: Prioritize explicit effect classes and commit/frontier gating for irreversible actions; evaluate recovery on task success plus leak/residue/stale-write/conflict and cost, not success alone.

long_horizon.o_fit: O's replay and idempotency records bind exact requests, but a restored model can synthesize semantically equivalent new requests; this is a direct adversarial failure mode for recovery.
long_horizon.scope: ACRFence attack validation: 10/10 checkpoint-restore trials duplicate commits versus 0/10 no-checkpoint; stateless single-use token validation permits 2/2 reuse attempts while stateful revocation rejects them.
long_horizon.uncertainty: The paper validates attacks, not the proposed ACRFence defense; simulated external services and tested CLI/model setup bound the result.
long_horizon.decision_use: Add semantic post-restore divergence/effect-ledger tests and require server-side durable revocation/settlement where applicable; do not claim checkpoint restore reverses external reality.

long_horizon.o_fit: O has source clocks, provenance, typed directives, and effect gates; MemTX's staged memory write versus committed belief state is a close operational analogue for preventing unverified state from authorizing effects.
long_horizon.scope: MemTX conformance-style suite over five backbones plus model checking of 5.5M protocol states; main tasks are short (1–4 turns, median 2).
long_horizon.uncertainty: Zero downstream harm in the reported suite and model-checked invariants do not establish long-horizon capability gains or general safety; evidence is governance/conformance oriented.
long_horizon.decision_use: Compare a staged optional-context/belief commit boundary against current direct admission for mutable state, preserving exact provenance and typed cascading invalidation.

long_horizon.o_fit: O's Context Kernel intentionally reduces materialized context; hidden retrieval/tool reacquisition cost is therefore a direct falsification metric for context selection/compression.
long_horizon.scope: Controlled 24-turn planning study across three models×two regimes; at 5× compression completion changes are nonsignificant while GPT-5.5 retrieval calls rise 21.0→63.9 (p=.002); irrelevant replacement raises retrieval 57%.
long_horizon.uncertainty: ALFWorld sliding compression does not show the same retrieval surge, so the reacquisition tax is environment dependent and not intrinsic to compression.
long_horizon.decision_use: Score context policies on terminal success plus retrieval/tool calls, elapsed steps, budget exhaustion, and reacquisition; reject 'same completion' as sufficient evidence of better context economics.

long_horizon.o_fit: O currently needs evidence that its selected context preserves actual next actions; TRACE directly measures local action continuity at compression boundaries rather than summary fact retention.
long_horizon.scope: AppWorld paired pre/post-compaction continuations over 590 boundaries/4,640 rollouts; summary approaches can increase immediate blocked/error and refetch/replay actions. TRACE improves prior compressed baselines but often remains below full context.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Results depend on budget/model/environment; unchanged transfer to Kimi can improve some metrics while MiniMax retains a substantial gap. It does not prove one universal compression template.
long_horizon.decision_use: Add boundary-local paired action tests around context projection changes, measuring first-action validity and multi-run reliability before treating semantic summary quality as success.

continual_learning.o_fit: Infinite-learning-rate scheduling is weight-training specific and O has no current matched continual-pretraining substrate; current decision bottlenecks are behavioral/evaluation/effect-control rather than optimizer schedules.
continual_learning.scope: Singh et al. continual pretraining under reset-between-dataset AdamW states; replay metrics and four-task retention gains are reported under those protocols.
continual_learning.uncertainty: No no-reset optimizer experiment was found; the dynamic-replay appendix changes both timing and old-domain composition, so timing is confounded. Transfer to O's current non-weight loop is untested.
continual_learning.decision_use: Retain as later training-substrate evidence; do not spend current O execution budget on it absent a concrete weight-update route.

continual_learning.o_fit: Online sample selection could matter if O adopts continual instruction/weight tuning, but current O primarily selects semantic context and experiments rather than minibatch training data.
continual_learning.scope: OASIS LLaMA-3.1-8B continual instruction tuning with last-layer-gradient selection and text/multimodal streams; text-only held-out improvements are reported at 6.25% selection.
continual_learning.uncertainty: The paper is internally inconsistent about 'forward-only' language, the linked official code repository is currently empty, and no explicit task-free evaluation was found.
continual_learning.decision_use: Keep separate from Context Kernel routing; revisit only with a training substrate and reproducible artifact, while preserving the computation/artifact caveats.

continual_learning.o_fit: Replay/gradient-alignment continual pretraining is not a current O mechanism and would require a substantial weight-training path before becoming decision actionable.
continual_learning.scope: Abbes et al. 1B five-task continual pretraining with uninterrupted optimizer state and effectively unbounded disk-backed replay; replay remains qualitatively strong in five-task extension.
continual_learning.uncertainty: Five-task figure lacks exact numeric table values; 560M downstream Average(en) values are internally inconsistent in the primary paper and must remain quarantined; replay is not constrained-memory evidence.
continual_learning.decision_use: Do not use the inconsistent 560M averages or visually estimated bars; revisit only for a concrete matched training decision.

continual_learning.o_fit: Task-free change-point detection and adapter routing has conceptual overlap with situation-dependent context routing, but HESTIA changes trainable adapters and is not yet quantified enough for current O.
continual_learning.scope: UAI 2026 HESTIA: order-invariant linearized adaptation, density-guided change-point detection, dynamic adapters, and likelihood routing with public code; exact paper tables/ablations were not yet extracted by the worker.
continual_learning.uncertainty: No current quantitative candidate table was verified in the clean artifact; transfer from adapter selection to semantic O Skills is hypothetical.
continual_learning.decision_use: Hold as a frontier candidate until exact task-free/error/parameter-cost ablations are available; do not promote architecture based on mechanism description alone.

multi_agent.o_fit: O seeks heterogeneous search but should not pay for nominally separate agents if one inference can produce more decorrelated candidates at lower cost.
multi_agent.scope: ACL 2026 divergent-thinking experiments match perspectives and output count; single-invocation multi-output is most diverse while multiple parallel agents are weakest, with MI-SO token cost reaching 8.49× at k=16 relative to SI-MO.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Scope is divergent/open-ended idea generation; it does not cover decomposable tool work, distinct information, different models, or independently isolated evaluation, where true multiplicity can add value.
multi_agent.decision_use: When parallel search is considered, require a measurable independent-information channel beyond role labels and compare against single-call multi-output at matched output/cost.

multi_agent.o_fit: O explicitly optimizes elapsed time and optional recursive work/context depth; conditional escalation is directly compatible with its routing architecture.
multi_agent.scope: ACL 2026 LAS versus fixed AFLOW on MBPP/HumanEval/GSM8K: roughly 37–63% token and 37–42% latency reductions for 0.5–1.4 pp accuracy cost. Gate-only MBPP falls to 86.7% versus AFLOW 94.2%.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Results are code/reasoning workflows, not arbitrary O graphs or team-size control. Cheap gating alone is unsafe; scheduler errors still cause harm.
multi_agent.decision_use: Treat additional stages/agents as escalation resources: measure marginal expected value of the next stage and preserve a stronger scheduler/verifier for uncertain cases.

multi_agent.o_fit: Semi-isolated lineages may help O's heterogeneous method search, but O is not currently an island-population runtime and simpler search controls are more immediately actionable.
multi_agent.scope: EvoPH TSP/bin-packing heuristic evolution; removing island model plus elite selection worsens all six reported heuristic cases.
multi_agent.uncertainty: The ablation removes island structure and elite selection together, so migration/local-archive causal credit and optimal migration cadence are unresolved; classical migration results are only a prior.
multi_agent.decision_use: Retain as a future search-population Candidate only if O enters population evolution; require matched isolation/migration cadence ablations.

multi_agent.o_fit: O often chooses among noisy candidate/evaluator outputs; Bayesian pairwise uncertainty and targeted comparison budget can improve search when a calibrated scalar reward is unavailable.
multi_agent.scope: Duel-Evolve test-time discrete-output optimization reports +20 points on MathBench and >12 over comparable iterative methods on LiveCodeBench using Bradley-Terry posterior plus Double Thompson Sampling.
multi_agent.uncertainty: No controlled evaluator-noise threshold was verified; same-model self-preferences and discrete test-time search may not transfer to O's heterogeneous evidence classes.
multi_agent.decision_use: Test uncertainty-aware pairwise allocation against equal/static judging at fixed evaluation cost; retain abstention when the judge posterior is not discriminating.

evaluation.o_fit: O's Candidate selection and future Best-of-N/reranking can fail even if a judge looks adequate on pairwise items; exact downstream selection-mode validation is decision critical.
evaluation.scope: REFLECT controlled research-agent failure alternatives; pairwise-to-Best-of-N process selection collapses to 0% for all four tested judges, with outcome selection dropping 14.5–34.5 pp.
evaluation.uncertainty: This does not prove every reranker fails; group construction, N, and research-agent failure taxonomy bound the result.
evaluation.decision_use: Meta-evaluate evaluators in the exact selection mode and N used by O, not only on isolated pairwise accuracy.

evaluation.o_fit: A learned global judge-reliability weight could help if O uses juries where labels are absent, but current O also has stronger mechanically judged paths for many protected decisions.
evaluation.scope: ICML 2026 SummEval/Topical-Chat pairwise assessment; BT-sigma reliability correlates with external judge performance and cycle consistency and improves SRC versus equal averaging at 2–8 judges.
evaluation.uncertainty: Reliability is global per judge and may miss instance-specific difficulty; transfer to agent trajectories/process/citation judgments is untested.
evaluation.decision_use: Use only as a jury-specific Candidate, paired with per-instance diagnostics; do not replace mechanical evaluation where available.

evaluation.o_fit: O's clean research intake requires traceable primary evidence; source relevance and factual support are separate failure surfaces and should not be collapsed into one verifier score.
evaluation.scope: 2026 citation-verifier benchmark with 624 attribution-citation pairs, 1,248 criterion decisions, 378 adjudicated hard cases; criterion rankings and directional errors differ and cost spans ~49×.
evaluation.uncertainty: Hard cases are disagreement-enriched rather than deployment prevalence; the best verifier/criterion can vary by domain.
evaluation.decision_use: Calibrate source relevance and factual support separately, report directional FPR/FNR/pass-rate drift, and escalate disagreement rather than using one aggregate citation score.

evaluation.o_fit: O and the external research pipeline can increase search depth; evidence shows deeper retrieval can preserve surface citation metrics while degrading factual support.
evaluation.scope: Two-model deep-research ablation over max tool calls 2→150: GPT-5.4 factual support 78.6%→16.7%, Claude Opus 4.6 80.0%→57.9%, while links/relevance remain high.
evaluation.uncertainty: The ablation does not isolate report length/source count/task difficulty and involves only two models; exact slope is not universal.
evaluation.decision_use: Stress-test research/report synthesis versus retrieval depth and cap/escalate when marginal evidence reduces factual support or verification coverage.

evaluation.o_fit: Abstention with calibrated accepted-set risk is directly relevant to O's `UNCERTAIN`/`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` policy and can prevent forced low-confidence decisions.
evaluation.scope: SCOPE pairwise judging on MT-Bench/RewardBench/Chatbot Arena: in-distribution empirical risk is typically ~.097–.099 at alpha=.10 with useful coverage; cross-benchmark transfer can rise to .157–.203.
evaluation.uncertainty: Guarantees rely on calibration/exchangeability and do not automatically cover O's multicriterion trajectories or distribution shift.
evaluation.decision_use: Prefer calibrated abstention over raw-confidence thresholds, and recalibrate under target-distribution shift rather than transferring a threshold blindly.

evaluation.o_fit: Aggregate judge quality can hide difficult individual cases; O needs case-level uncertainty to decide when to escalate or abstain.
evaluation.scope: SummEval study: aggregate 3-cycle rates 0.8–4.1% yet 33–67% of documents contain a cycle; conformal rating-set width correlates with judge-human error at Spearman .576 over N=1,918.
evaluation.uncertainty: Validated on NLG criteria, not O's tool traces; cycle repair itself did not improve human ranking agreement, so the signal is diagnostic rather than a guaranteed fix.
evaluation.decision_use: Add per-instance uncertainty/consistency diagnostics to any learned judge and route wide/high-cycle cases to stronger or mechanical evidence.

evaluation.o_fit: O's strict scope policy still needs a principled way to call small observed deltas unresolved when the benchmark lacks power; this is directly decision changing.
evaluation.scope: Resolution Diagnostics reports 11/40 Open LLM Leaderboard v1 comparisons and 4/9 adjacent MMLU-Pro top-10 pairs unresolved at alpha=.05/power=.8; clustering raises MMLU-Pro to 6/9.
evaluation.uncertainty: Worker extraction is abstract-level pending full primary-table verification; binary/accuracy paired formulas require adaptation for O's graded/multilevel outcomes.
evaluation.decision_use: Compute paired, cluster-aware resolution/MDE before interpreting small Candidate regressions or gains; emit unresolved rather than directional claims below resolution.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O's active action-adherence unit already rejects verbal/terminal-only evidence; this worker supplies direct evidence that outcome-only scoring can credit procedurally invalid success and reverse rankings.
failure_evidence.scope: τ-bench Retail/Airline, GPT-5/Kimi-K2/Mistral, four trials/task. Applying six procedure-aware gates lowers success materially and yields 27–78% 'corrupt successes' in the reported study.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: The six binary gates are not uniquely correct deployment metrics and automatic judge precision is high but not perfect; corruption rates are benchmark/model specific.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Keep terminal outcome and procedural/action validity separate, validate the procedural judge itself, and test whether ranking changes under policy-faithful scoring.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O's Candidate evidence can be misleading if it relies on single trajectories; repeated same-task outcome consistency directly informs confidence and regression policy.
failure_evidence.scope: ICML 2026 reliability study: 15 models on GAIA and verified τ-bench Airline with K=5 runs/task; moderate/high accuracy can coexist with much lower same-task consistency.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Two model cells cannot expose temperature-zero controls and include provider-default stochasticity; one scaffold per benchmark and verified subset limit transfer.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Require repeated-run distributions/consistency for stochastic or provider-mediated capabilities, not only average success or best-run evidence.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O's Context Kernel already treats effect dispatch as a critical boundary; the evidence says deviations at mutating actions are disproportionately associated with failure.
failure_evidence.scope: SABER traces on τ-bench Airline/Retail and SWE-Bench Verified; each additional mutating-action deviation is associated with up to 92%/96% lower odds of success in the reported models, while non-mutating deviations have little effect.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Logistic association is not proof every mutating deviation causes failure; 'up to' effect sizes are benchmark/model specific.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Weight evaluation and pre-dispatch safeguards toward state-mutating actions and side-effect boundaries rather than treating every trace mismatch as equally causal.

reasoning.o_fit: Search-policy support/diversity is relevant to O's heterogeneous exploration, but the mechanism is post-training in Lean and not an immediate O substrate.
reasoning.scope: ICLR 2026 Lean proof policy: Base 54.2/86.0 pass@1/pass@256, GRPO 71.5/81.0, alpha-DPG α=.5 61.4/88.5, α=.999 73.0/83.5.
reasoning.uncertainty: Diversity/pass@K correlations are not a causal gate and higher diversity trades against pass@1; Lean/proof-training scope is narrow.
reasoning.decision_use: Use as evidence that precision and coverage are separate search objectives; defer training adoption until O has a matched trainable policy path.

reasoning.o_fit: O already changes methods after stalled evidence; a learned continue-versus-restart router from failed trajectories directly targets elapsed-time optimization.
reasoning.scope: Lean PutnamBench subset of 85 problems with Goedel-Prover-V2-8B; current v3 reports 28.9% average cost reduction versus fixed-step baseline at approximately preserved performance.
reasoning.uncertainty: One backend and benchmark subset; router calibration/generalization outside theorem proving is unresolved.
reasoning.decision_use: Test failure-conditioned continuation/restart decisions at O logical-unit boundaries against fixed budgets, using actual future cost and outcome rather than static heuristics.

reasoning.o_fit: O's reversible Candidate logic can layer learned interventions after a reliable baseline fails instead of globally replacing a competent mechanism.
reasoning.scope: Lean 4 `grind`: cost-aware e-match filtering ~5% faster and +2 theorems; failure-triggered split lookahead proves 5 stock-timeout theorems with no regressions to stock-solved cases by cascade construction.
reasoning.uncertainty: Absolute gains are modest and specific to grind internals; static split models failing does not prove runtime lookahead is universally superior.
reasoning.decision_use: Prefer baseline→failure trigger→bounded probe when interventions can be non-monotone; compare against always-on activation at matched cost.

reasoning.o_fit: Even machine-checked outputs do not validate benchmark formalization; O's evidence integrity requires benchmark/harness auditing before trusting small deltas.
reasoning.scope: ICML 2026 Lean audit: 10,318 problems, 4,833 static-checker findings, 398 mechanically certified issues; corrected subsets can inflate or deflate prover scores.
reasoning.uncertainty: A static finding is not automatically a semantic defect; scope is audited Lean benchmark families and exact versions.
reasoning.decision_use: Pin benchmark/toolchain versions, use audited subsets/checkers where feasible, and compare claimed gains to benchmark-defect/resolution uncertainty.

reasoning.o_fit: Diversity-preserving training plus verifier sharpening is potentially useful, but O currently lacks a Lean/post-training route and has more immediate evaluation bottlenecks.
reasoning.scope: LeanWorkbook: Feedback Distillation + GRPO reported 75% pass@1 versus 59% GRPO alone; training uses 10k statements and Claude Opus 4.6 feedback.
reasoning.uncertainty: Exact pass@K/entropy curves remain pending worker verification; teacher cost/dependence and Lean-specificity are material.
reasoning.decision_use: Retain as future training evidence; do not infer O-wide benefit from the reported combination result.

reasoning.o_fit: O can benefit from diversity-aware search, but CARTS gains are small and theorem-prover/tree-search specific compared with more general current bottlenecks.
reasoning.scope: ICLR 2025 miniF2F/ProofNet fixed-policy search; full CARTS gives modest pass-rate gains across several backbones, with non-additive components and one-step-tree scope.
reasoning.uncertainty: Adjustment heuristic is not uniformly beneficial; multi-step integration and compute-normalized execution savings are unresolved.
reasoning.decision_use: Use as a scoped search-control candidate only when O has a comparable branch-search problem; require cost-normalized ablation.

reasoning.o_fit: Predicting environment effects/error/time before spending verifier budget maps well to O's goal of allocating search to independently useful branches rather than surface-diverse text.
reasoning.scope: NeurIPS 2025 Lean: transition-aware DPP tactic subset improves miniF2F pass@1 most at K=8 (22.4→24.4 vs Top-K) with smaller gains as K grows; LeanDojo Novel Premises 31.3→32.3 at K=32.
reasoning.uncertainty: More diversity can reduce pass@1; benefit shrinks when filtering is weak. It is not yet combined with compiler-guided repair or shown cross-domain.
reasoning.decision_use: Test predicted effect/outcome diversity as a branch-allocation feature only where execution budget is scarce, and compare to quality-only/top-K at fixed cost.

open_source.o_fit: O's optional-context routing currently emphasizes admission/selection; this update shows negative transfer may depend more on memory abstraction and utilization contract than a simple retrieval threshold.
open_source.scope: Public Memento and ReasoningBank code both force top-k/nearest retrieval when memory exists. ReasoningBank instead stores generalized success/failure principles and lets the model consider relevance; published results show up to 20% relative effectiveness and 16% fewer steps in its own settings.
open_source.uncertainty: The EvoAgentBench third-party adapter/config is not public, so its severe Memento regression cannot be causally attributed to the inspected retrieval path; ReasoningBank versus Memento abstraction/utilization difference is not isolated by matched ablation.
open_source.decision_use: Factor context-memory tests into retrieval unit (concrete case vs generalized principle), injection/utilization discretion, and admission threshold; keep a no-memory fallback and do not overcredit thresholding alone.

scientist_agents.o_fit: O actively chooses search methods and budgets; same-model scaffold comparisons show workflow/search structure can change research performance independently of base model.
scientist_agents.scope: AIRS same-model Greedy versus One-Shot average normalized score deltas range +.161 to +.323 across six reported model backbones; AI Scientist node budget 5→32 raises automated-review score 3.30→3.93.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: Greedy-versus-ReAct is confounded by different harness limits/splits/scoring; node scaling does not isolate topology from compute and uses an automated reviewer outcome.
scientist_agents.decision_use: When comparing research/search scaffolds, hold model and evaluation semantics fixed and measure a compute curve rather than attributing gains to topology or more nodes by default.

scientist_agents.o_fit: O's expected-time objective needs explicit compute scaling curves because more search can improve a proxy while resource use remains a poor ordering of scientific quality.
scientist_agents.scope: Worker synthesis contrasts AI Scientist within-workflow node scaling with MLReplicate cross-system evidence that resource use does not reliably order human scientific quality.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: The two evidence sets are not a matched causal comparison and the AI Scientist outcome is automated review, not independently validated scientific truth.
scientist_agents.decision_use: Separate architecture, compute budget, and evaluator quality in O research-method decisions; demand marginal decision value per added compute.

scientist_agents.o_fit: Structured multi-hypothesis failure attribution plus independent criticism and hierarchy-aware repair routing directly addresses O's need to localize why an experiment failed before changing the wrong layer.
scientist_agents.scope: SAGE 12-topic five-domain ARC-Bench subset: metric-bearing recovery 5/12→11/12 versus same-harness reflection; AR-Eval 5.00→6.75; blind ML PhD review 3.00→5.67; component ablations reportedly make MHFA the largest degradation.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: Small sample, human review only on six ML topics, and replication/cost accounting across independent harnesses are missing; correlated critic/generator errors remain unresolved.
scientist_agents.decision_use: Test multi-hypothesis failure localization as an explicit diagnostic Candidate before repair, scoring whether it improves correct-layer intervention and final outcome at matched cost.

scientist_agents.o_fit: EviGraph's typed evidence-dependency state, weak-node localization, transactional downstream regeneration, and claim-readiness gate closely match O's provenance/dependency architecture but add a research-specific causal repair target.
scientist_agents.scope: ARC-Bench-ML package-level results report 86.45% overall research performance versus ~60.37% strongest compared baseline and Claim Support Rate 37.85% versus 27%.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: No component-level ablation was verified; seeds, budgets, judge dependence, rollback frequency, and repair-memory contribution remain unresolved, and 37.85% claim support is low in absolute terms.
scientist_agents.decision_use: Use as a candidate for evidence-graph-driven localization/repair only after extracting component ablations; do not infer the graph alone caused the system-level gain.

scientist_agents.o_fit: Executable intermediate representations plus layered syntax/fidelity/simulation gates offer a concrete pattern for turning natural-language scientific plans into checkable actions, but the demonstrated domain is chemistry reproduction rather than general O work.
scientist_agents.scope: ACRA: 150 ChemRnD procedures, 99.33% syntactically valid XDL and 94.67% passing later source-discrepancy/hardware-simulation validation; six real syntheses on two robotic platforms; memory/data ablation 85.3→93.3% late-stage success.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: Evidence is faithful procedure translation/execution, not open-ended discovery; source-fidelity judge quality, no-critique ablation, and domains lacking mature DSLs remain unresolved; two tested open models up to 70B failed valid XDL generation.
scientist_agents.decision_use: Consider executable IR + layered verification only for O subdomains with a trustworthy formal/action schema; keep language-level scientific claims outside syntax/executability proof.

cross_field.o_fit: O allocates finite evaluation/search budgets; asymptotic concentration rules can be actively worse when evidence is sparse, so a budget/confidence regime is decision relevant.
cross_field.scope: Ranking-and-selection evidence: in one 10-design feasibility example classical asymptotic allocation does not surpass equal allocation until total budget >~3000; modern budget-adaptive OCBA derives a distinct finite-budget T=O(k log k) regime.
cross_field.uncertainty: The ~3000 crossover is example-specific and asymptotic scaling is not a universal finite switch threshold; transfer to O requires observable confidence/error estimates.
cross_field.decision_use: Start broad under sparse evidence and progressively concentrate only as confidence/budget grows; compare adaptive allocation against equal/racing/static concentration at matched total evaluation cost.

cross_field.o_fit: O already checkpoints and recovers, but semantic/dependency-risk-triggered persistence could reduce rollback depth without checkpointing every small action.
cross_field.scope: 1993 iPSC/860 distributed-system experiment: adaptive independent checkpointing reduced average rollback to <1 state interval per process with ~10% more checkpoints than periodic independent checkpointing.
cross_field.uncertainty: Old message-passing hardware and rollback-consistency semantics differ sharply from modern agent/workflow state; transfer is a hypothesis, not direct O evidence.
cross_field.decision_use: If checkpoint overhead is material, test event/dependency-risk-triggered checkpoints against fixed cadence on actual O lost-work/recovery metrics.

cross_field.o_fit: O often has cheaper proxy tasks or related experiments; choosing them by information about the expensive target per unit cost directly serves the elapsed-time objective.
cross_field.scope: Multi-task Bayesian optimization: target MNIST validation minimum reached in ~40 versus ~100 minutes using cheaper USPS queries; LDA target minimum in ~6 versus ~10 days using cheaper 50k-document task.
cross_field.uncertainty: Task correlation must be learned; direct source-optimum transfer can fail, and later negative-transfer evidence warns standard MTGPs can misestimate relatedness.
cross_field.decision_use: Use proxy experiments only with explicit target-correlation diagnostics and a target-only fallback; optimize expected target information per cost rather than proxy score.

neuroscience.o_fit: Local biologically constrained credit assignment is not on O's current execution path and does not address the immediate behavioral/evaluation/external-evidence bottlenecks.
neuroscience.scope: 2026 DTP supervised vision evidence with five-instance setups: DTP trails matched EIANN-BP by 2.57–4.70 pp in recovered FMNIST/CIFAR conditions; absolute CIFAR accuracy is low.
neuroscience.uncertainty: S3/S4 use symmetric feedback; asymmetric-feedback evidence is separate MNIST only; no independent exact replication was found and 'comparable to BP' is not parity.
neuroscience.decision_use: Keep as long-horizon training research, not a current O Candidate unless a local-credit weight-training substrate becomes relevant.

neuroscience.o_fit: Hierarchical modular recurrence/cycle structure could inform memory/search topology, but current evidence uses fixed reservoirs with linear readouts and simple memory/multitask tasks rather than O's semantic engine.
neuroscience.scope: Nature Communications 2026 synthetic graph perturbation/null controls plus connectome analysis: higher hierarchy/cycle-preserving controls improve reservoir memory and multitasking across reported regimes.
neuroscience.uncertainty: Third hierarchy level rarely adds over second; cycles explain memory substantially but not all multitasking benefit; no independent replication and no end-to-end trainable-agent transfer were established.
neuroscience.decision_use: Retain as a cross-architecture hypothesis; require matched trainable RNN/transformer/agent evidence before giving it O implementation priority.
